criteria.note: Every clause AC1 states about points, raw columns, reasons and the roll-up was driven and reddened the row that names it. Ten mutations: the point scaled off the tokens/peg ratio (AC1 headline row red), the raw token column rounded to the nearest 100 and the recorded cost column scaled 100x (the non-round-value row red for each), the point gate swapped to the corpus spend_recorded flag so a cost-only change prints 0.000 pt (the confident-zero row and its control red), the recorded-zero reason collapsed into the nothing-recorded reason (the fourth-shape row and the four-distinct-reasons row red), the recorded cost appended to every line ROUNDED to 12.4 and, separately, the recorded 7.50 moved into the money column of the token-less row (the complete-figure-list row red for each, which is the one instrument here that a literal-absence check could not have replaced), and points_total replaced by a raw-token figure (the whole-dict roll-up row red). The four-shape taxonomy, the shipped-writer fixture and the mtime_ns guard on the live log are real. TWO GAPS BEYOND ITS LITERAL WORDS, both reported as findings rather than as a refutation: a MEASURED change renders as `0.000 pt` once the peg is more than about 2000x its tokens, and the guard for that string is scoped to one fixture whose ratios cannot produce it (F4); and the money column prints 0.00 usd for a change whose recorded cost is 7.50, which the suite pins (F7).

Seven mutations, seven named rows red, and the two isolation mutations are the ones worth naming. Taking the middle element of the INPUT order instead of the sorted counts is invisible on the base fixture and reddens the 'moving ONE recorded count MOVES THE PEG' row alone, so that row really does prove the median is computed. Taking the UPPER median is identical on every odd sample and reddens the even-sample lower-median row. Also driven with teeth: the risk filter removed, a fabricated peg of 1 token where the corpus supports none, the declared-era check removed, the refusal no longer reported, and a malformed declared peg falling back to the derivation. One minor gap: a DECLARED peg is not required to name a spec, so the render prints 'spec None' while the module's own rationale for the lower median is that a reader can open the peg (F13).

The property holds and two of its three legs have teeth. Making normalize mutate the corpus record it was handed reddens the byte-identity row; scaling the point cell by the supplied price reddens the price row; making normalize touch the repository's real event log reddens the live row's mtime_ns clause. NOTE ON WHAT THE FIXTURE LEG CAN SEE, reported rather than treated as a defect: resolve_peg, normalize and render_lines never receive a path, so the event-log bytes and the seeded spec bytes cannot change under any mutation of the three functions under test; those two clauses are structurally true rather than measured, and the write-detection tooth lives in the live leg instead. The two-views-must-DIFFER and tampered-comparator legs are in-suite controls by design; no module mutation can make the views identical without also reddening AC1 or AC2, which is the correct shape for a control.

The era rules are real: overwriting an existing ledger entry, giving a cross-era row a point, pegging to the EARLIEST era instead of the latest, and folding the straddle reason together with the unreadable-timestamp reason each reddened the row that names them. THREE THINGS AGAINST IT, all reported as findings. (1) The round-trip leg fails as a CRASH, not a red: dropping previous_model from the written key order raises KeyError at fragment line 710, exit 1 with no suite summary and every later fragment in manifest order unrun (F11). (2) The headline 'TWO ERAS ARE NEVER BLENDED' is false about the printed roll-up: tokens_total sums raw tokens across eras and the bottom line presents 5000 raw tokens over ['era-two','pre-ledger'] with no qualification, and view_e's whole-dict equality PINS a 24000 blended total (F5). (3) The straddle rule is decided by every spend event, not by the token events, so a change whose token spend is wholly inside the peg's era is refused with the reason 'this total is itself a mixture of units' because of one human_minutes event on the other side of the shift (F6). The criterion's literal words survive (3) and its enumerated selftests all have teeth, which is why this is confirmed with notes rather than refuted.

Both blockers live here. FIRST: the fail-closed claim is unevidenced for the shape that reaches it. The only bad neighbours in the fixture are a record outside the PARSER subset and a second shift at the same instant, so the validate_shift refusal INSIDE load_ledger is never exercised. Making load_ledger accept every malformed record into the ledger and report nothing left the suite at 60 passed, 0 failed; so did emptying the whole ledger on the first bad record, which is the 'half applied' catastrophe the module's own docstring calls worse than none; so did removing the duplicate-era-id refusal. SECOND: 'NO GATE STAGE CONSULTS THIS MODULE' is a substring scan over scripts/verify.sh's text and cannot fail for the defect it names. I added a real stage to validate.run_all that loads toe_normalize, builds the view and reddens the gate when no peg is in force; `.veldo/validate.py all` then exits 1 printing '.veldo/toe_normalize.py: the normalized planning view has no peg in force', and the suite stayed at 60 passed, 0 failed. PLAN-0014 NG1 is the plan's hard boundary and this is the assertion that guards it. What IS solid in AC5: the eight hostile shapes each refuse by name with the all() bound to its own literal list, the well-formed record validates clean, the same-instant refusal fires, and the absent-directory path is asserted as an EMPTY message list rather than a count.

findings.text: AC5's fail-closed branch has no teeth. load_ledger refuses a malformed record through `report` and leaves it out; NO fixture in the suite puts a record that PARSES but fails validate_shift beside a good one, so that entire branch is undriven. Three separate mutations of it leave the suite fully green: accepting every malformed record into the ledger while reporting nothing, returning an EMPTY ledger on the first bad record (which silently deletes every era and every row's era), and removing the duplicate-era-id refusal. The shipped code is correct today and nothing would notice it stopping being correct. This is the dominant PLAN-0018 shape: a check that cannot fail for the defect its own criterion names.

findings.text: AC5's 'NO GATE STAGE CONSULTS THIS MODULE' is proven with `'toe_normalize' not in scripts/verify.sh`, a substring scan over one file's text, and the property it claims is about the gate's STAGES. verify.sh does not name the modules validate.py loads, so a stage added inside validate.run_all is invisible to it. I added such a stage: it loads toe_normalize by path, builds the view over the repository and calls fail() when no peg is in force. The gate then exits 1 on a planning number, which is exactly what PLAN-0014 NG1 forbids and what this criterion exists to prevent, and the suite stayed 60 passed / 0 failed. Fourth recorded appearance of the substring-scan family after ledger findings 48, 50 and 56, and finding 63 already prescribes the fix shape for this exact assertion: make the SUBJECT the gate's own stages, derived from validate.run_all's module loads plus the stage scripts verify.sh names.

findings.text: SHIPPING THIS NOW DELIVERS A TRACEBACK, NOT A CAPABILITY, AND THIS IS THE FINDING THAT DECIDES THE SHIP QUESTION. Removing the four-module exclusion from scripts/publish.py puts engine/.veldo/toe_normalize.py in the pack, but .veldo/init_scaffold.py lays down 28 .veldo modules and NONE of toe_normalize.py, toe_corpus.py, metrics.py or spend.py. In a repository scaffolded by the shipped installer, the documented entry point exits 1 with FileNotFoundError on .veldo/toe_corpus.py. PLAN-0018 finding 61 verbatim, in a new module, and finding 44's rule in mirror image. Three more halves of the same capability are also missing: .veldo/capabilities.yaml declares toe_ground_truth_corpus and spend_recording and nothing for normalization, no document in docs/ or README.md mentions Tokens of Effort at all, and no veldo CLI verb reaches the module. All four are WARP-1410's declared scope (W10: 'so /veldo:init lays them down and the packs carry them; make the docs true; record capabilities honestly'), and specs/index.md lists W10 as waiting on this item among six others. An adopter receives a fragment.

findings.text: A MEASURED CHANGE RENDERS AS `0.000 pt`, the exact string AC1 forbids, and the guard against it is scoped to one fixture whose ratios cannot produce it. round(tokens/peg, 3) is 0.0 for any ratio under 0.0005, which is an ordinary spread in an agent-run repository (a few hundred tokens against a peg of a few hundred thousand). Worse for the planner: points_total sums the ROUNDED points, so such a change contributes exactly zero to the bottom line a plan is sized with. The suite's protection is `'0.000 pt' not in ''.join(render_lines(view_h))`, and fixture H's smallest ratio is 0.041.
findings.evidence: Shipped code, no mutation. Peg 300000 (WARP-8001), a 3-token change: 'WARP-8003          0.000 pt          3 tok       0.01 usd' with reason null, counted inside 'total: 2.0 pt over 3 change(s)'. Second fixture, ten changes at 300000 and five at 100 tokens: peg 300000 sample 15, the five measured 100-token rows each render '0.000 pt        100 tok' and points_total is reported as 10.0 where the true sum of ratios is 10.001667. FIX SHAPE: render a below-resolution point as '<0.001 pt' or carry the unrounded ratio into points_total, and assert it over a fixture whose spread produces one.

findings.text: THE RAW-TOKEN ROLL-UP BLENDS ERAS, WHICH IS THE ONE THING AC4's HEADLINE FORBIDS, AND THE SUITE PINS THE BLEND. summary()['tokens_total'] sums r['tokens'] over ALL rows regardless of era, and the printed bottom line puts that figure beside a list of the eras present with no qualification, so the number a planner reads as the raw total is, by this module's own doctrine, 'a number no model ever produced'. points_total correctly refuses to blend; the raw total it sits next to does not. The whole-dict equality that guards the roll-up asserts tokens_total 24000 for a two-era view, so the blend is not an oversight the suite could catch, it is the value the suite requires.
findings.evidence: Shipped code, no mutation. One shift at 2026-01-04, WARP-8101 at 1000 tokens in pre-ledger, WARP-8102 at 4000 in era-two: bottom line 'total: 1.0 pt over 1 change(s), 5000 raw tokens, 1 row(s) with no point, eras [era-two, pre-ledger]', summary {'tokens_total': 5000, 'eras_present': ['era-two','pre-ledger'], ...}. Suite line 771-774 pins the same shape: view_e summary tokens_total 24000 with eras_present ['era-second-model','pre-ledger']. FIX SHAPE: report tokens_total per era, or name the mixture in the bottom line the way every refused row names it.

findings.text: A NON-TOKEN SPEND EVENT DECIDES THE ERA OF A TOKEN MEASUREMENT, AND THE PRINTED REASON IS THEN FALSE. spend_ats() selects events by the corpus's spend_recorded predicate, which is true for cost_usd or human_minutes alone; that is the very flag recorded_tokens() exists to refuse on the point path, and it is used unqualified on the era path. So a change whose token spend was recorded wholly inside the peg's era loses its point because a human-minutes event sits on the other side of a shift, and the row says 'spend spans 2 eras, so this total is itself a mixture of units' about a token total that is not a mixture and about human minutes that are not denominated in tokens at all. Two spellings of one predicate, on a second path, which is the defect AC1's own text says one named predicate exists to prevent.
findings.evidence: Shipped code, no mutation. Shift at 2026-01-04; WARP-8301 = tokens 4000 at 2026-01-05 plus human_minutes 30 at 2026-01-02; WARP-8302 = tokens 4000 at 2026-01-06. Rendered: 'WARP-8301              - pt       4000 tok  (spend spans 2 eras (era-two, pre-ledger), so this total is itself a mixture of units and is not normalized)' while WARP-8302 gets 1.000 pt. era_of('WARP-8301', ...) -> (None, 'spend spans 2 eras ...'). Reachable through the sanctioned writer: .veldo/spend.py exposes --human-minutes and --cost-usd independently of --tokens. FIX SHAPE: derive the era from the events that carried the TOKEN count, through the same one predicate the point uses, and keep a separate honest note when other spend fields straddle.

findings.text: THE MONEY COLUMN PRINTS 0.00 usd FOR A CHANGE WHOSE RECORDED COST IS 7.50, AND THE SUITE PINS IT. AC1's decision not to print the recorded cost is sound; substituting a DERIVED zero for it is the confident zero one column over, in the money column, on the row whose whole message is that nothing was measured. The point column gets this right, printing '- pt'; the dollar column does not. The row's reason names tokens and says nothing about the dollar figure, so a reader scanning the money column sees a change that cost nothing.
findings.evidence: Shipped code, no mutation. WARP-8202 recorded cost_usd 7.5 and no tokens, rendered at 2.00 per 1k: 'WARP-8202              - pt          0 tok       0.00 usd  (spend was recorded in cost_usd but NOT in tokens, ...)'. The suite requires exactly this: _W1406_H_FIGS_050 / _400 pin ('WARP-9423', ['0', '0.00']) at both prices. FIX SHAPE: print the same '-' in the money column wherever the point column prints '-', since both are derived from a token count that does not exist.

findings.text: THE SAME-INSTANT REFUSAL COMPARES THE TIMESTAMP STRING, SO ONE INSTANT SPELLED TWO WAYS PASSES AND LEAVES A DECLARED ERA NOTHING CAN EVER BE IN. load_ledger keys seen_at on rec['at'] rather than on the parsed instant, so '2026-01-04T00:00:00Z' and '2026-01-04T00:00:00+00:00' are two boundaries to the ledger and one moment in time. Both records are accepted with ZERO problems reported, eras() then emits an interval that is half open on the right at its own left edge, and era_at returns the LATER era at the boundary and forever after. The earlier era is declared, listed in eras_declared, reported in the view, and unreachable. AC5's own words are that two shifts claiming one instant are refused 'because no actual at that instant would have one era'.
findings.evidence: Shipped code, no mutation. Two ledger files written through render_shift; parse_iso confirms the two values are the SAME instant (True); load_ledger -> 0 problems, [] messages, ledger accepted ['era-a','era-b']; eras() -> era-a from 2026-01-04T00:00:00Z to 2026-01-04T00:00:00+00:00; era_at('2026-01-03T23:59:59Z') = 'pre-ledger', era_at('2026-01-04T00:00:00Z') = 'era-b', era_at('2026-01-05T00:00:00Z') = 'era-b'. FIX SHAPE: key the duplicate-instant check on read_at(rec['at'], parse_iso), which the function already computes one line above for the sort.

findings.text: THE SPEC DECLARES NO FALSIFICATION FOR ANY CRITERION, SO NOBODY WAS EVER ASKED THE QUESTION THIS METHOD ASKS. specs/WARP-1406 carries no falsified_by field and no behavior_bearing field, so validate_checks' falsification gate treats it as exempt (absent is exempt) and stands down; the gate run records 168 such stand-downs, this item among them. WARP-1409, in the same plan and the same lane, declares eight. The consequence is not theoretical: this review had to derive all 34 mutations itself, and the two blockers above are precisely the mutations a declared falsification would have forced the author to build before claiming the criterion. An item held back from a release for want of an independent review should not also be the item that never declared what would refute it.

From the baseline gate run on the reviewed tree: 'falsification migration: 45 spec(s) declare behaviour of 213, 45 already comply, 0 would be refused, 168 stood down. Posture: REFUSING since 2026-08-11 (01bcdf3)'. Also measured: specs/index.md line 33 gives WARP-1406 status `ready` and line 440 lists it on the ready FRONTIER, and ls -d proof/WARP-140* returns nothing, so no PLAN-0014 item has a proof bundle at all and there is no per-criterion evidence record to audit this verdict against.

findings.text: THE LIVE-REPOSITORY LEG'S STATED ATTRIBUTION IS FALSE. Its own comment says the forced peg is there so 'the only thing left that can withhold a point is the token predicate'. It is not: era_of returns None for every one of the 174 rows because this repository's log carries no spend event at all, so the era branch withholds the point first. Defeating the token predicate outright (an unmeasured change getting 0.000 instead of None) leaves that row GREEN; only a mutation that bypasses every gate at once reddens it. The invariant is real and the row is not vacuous, but it does not measure what it says it measures, and a reader auditing the item would take it for the guard it is not.

findings.text: TWO DECLARED PROPERTIES FAIL AS A CRASH RATHER THAN A NAMED RED, AND THE CRASH TAKES THE WHOLE SELFTEST WITH IT. Exit is 1 in both cases, so the gate does redden, but no suite summary is printed and every fragment after this one in manifest order never runs, which is 19 suites of results replaced by a traceback. Same family as PLAN-0018 finding 54's uncaught TypeError, and the exact hazard .veldo/promises.py:173-175 documents about its own AC1.

findings.text: A NEGATIVE RECORDED TOKEN COUNT PRODUCES A SELF-CONTRADICTORY REASON, AND THE GATE'S EVENT VALIDATOR DOES NOT REFUSE ONE. spend_fields_recorded() names any field whose value is non-zero, including a negative token count, while recorded_tokens() refuses it, so the row reads 'spend was recorded in tokens but NOT in tokens'. The money column prints -0.01 usd beside it. .veldo/spend.py refuses negatives on its own path, but validate.check_events reports 0 problems for a log line carrying tokens: -5, so any other emitter reaches this.
findings.evidence: Shipped code, no mutation: 'WARP-8402              - pt         -5 tok      -0.01 usd  (spend was recorded in tokens but NOT in tokens, and a point is a ratio of tokens to tokens, so a point here would be a confident zero rather than a measurement)'. validate.check_events over a one-line log with tokens:-5 -> 0 problems. FIX SHAPE: name a field only when its value is a POSITIVE number, and give a negative its own reason.

findings.text: THE PEG CAN NAME NO CHANGE, AND A DERIVED PEG STANDS UP ON A SAMPLE OF ONE. validate_peg does not require `spec`, so a declared peg renders as 'spec None' while D1's stated reason for taking the lower median is that a planner can open the peg and read it; the suite's own live-forced leg passes spec=None. Separately, on the first real use of the feature the derived peg came back with sample 1 and was still presented as 'median_standard_risk_shipped' with three decimals of point precision on every row, with no stand-down and no widening, which sits awkwardly beside PLAN-0014 NG6 (an estimator that has not converged reports its own uncertainty). The sample IS disclosed on the line, which is why this is minor rather than major.
findings.evidence: Additive control C1, shipped CLI, on the review copy: python3 .veldo/spend.py record for three shipped specs, then python3 .veldo/toe_normalize.py peg -> {'basis': 'median_standard_risk_shipped', 'era': 'era-first-model', 'pegged': true, 'sample': 1, 'spec': 'WARP-1401', 'tokens': 208901}; the report's first line reads 'peg: 208901 tokens = 1.000 pt (median_standard_risk_shipped, era era-first-model, spec WARP-1401, sample 1)' and three rows carry points to three decimals. Suite line 939 passes spec=None deliberately.

summary: DO-NOT-SHIP, and FAIL as a review. The module is good work and most of it is genuinely proven: I derived and drove 34 falsifications (the spec declares none, see F9), and 27 reddened the row they name, including every clause of AC1's point-and-reason taxonomy, both peg-isolation mutations that prove the median is computed rather than picked, the purity property under a real re-peg, and the era refusals. THE SHIP ANSWER IS NO FOR ONE MEASURED REASON ABOVE ALL: in a repository scaffolded by the shipped installer, `python3 .veldo/toe_normalize.py report` exits 1 with FileNotFoundError on .veldo/toe_corpus.py, because init_scaffold lays down 28 modules and neither this one nor the two siblings it loads. Dropping the publish exclusion therefore ships a file, not a capability, with no capabilities.yaml entry, no document and no CLI verb either. All four are WARP-1410's declared scope, and W10 is still waiting on six other items. That is PLAN-0018 finding 61 reproduced in a new module (F3). THE REVIEW ANSWER IS FAIL ON TWO MORE BLOCKERS, both in AC5, both the ledger's dominant shape. Making load_ledger accept every malformed era record and report nothing leaves the suite at 60 passed / 0 failed, as does emptying the whole ledger on one bad record and as does removing the duplicate-id refusal: the branch AC5's fail-closed claim is about is never driven, because the fixture's only bad neighbours are a parse error and a same-instant duplicate (F1). And 'NO GATE STAGE CONSULTS THIS MODULE', the assertion guarding PLAN-0014's hard non-goal, is a substring scan over verify.sh's text: I added a real stage to validate.run_all that reddens the gate on a planning number, proved `.veldo/validate.py all` exits 1 with that refusal, and the suite stayed green (F2). Six majors beyond that, four of them wrong answers the suite currently blesses: a MEASURED change printing 0.000 pt and contributing exactly zero to the planner's bottom line (F4), a raw-token roll-up that blends eras while the points refuse to and a pinned 24000 that requires the blend (F5), a human-minutes event deciding the era of a token measurement and printing a false 'mixture of units' reason for it (F6), a money column reporting 0.00 usd for a change whose recorded cost is 7.50 (F7), one instant spelled two ways creating a declared era nothing can be in (F8), and no declared falsification anywhere in the spec (F9). The good news worth recording: the additive control passes cleanly. Recording a capability shift through the shipped CLI and three real spends through the shipped writer leaves the suite at 60 passed / 0 failed and produces a correct view (peg WARP-1401 at 208901 tokens, three pointed rows, 171 standing down with reasons), so nothing here pins this repository's current emptiness and using the feature does not redden the gate. Fix F1, F2, F4, F5, F6, F7 and F8, declare the falsifications, and land the lay-down, capability and document halves with W10; then this ships.
